program_name: Cellular and Molecular Biology (official English name used on apply.unito.it and on the programme microsite; the full Italian/bilingual official title in the UNITO catalogue is 'CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY - BIOLOGIA CELLULARE E MOLECOLARE'). UNITO internal degree-programme code [2201M22]; MUR 'codicione' 0010107300700011; apply.unito.it course id 345; en.unito.it degree ids 45018 (current a.y.) and 39718 (earlier a.y.). The degree is coordinated by the Department of Life Sciences and Systems Biology (Dipartimento di Scienze della Vita e Biologia dei Sistemi, DBIOS) within the School of Natural Sciences (Scuola di Scienze della Natura). Commonly abbreviated 'CMB' on its own microsite and e-learning platform (cmb.i-learn.unito.it).
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale). apply.unito.it lists 'Type: POSTGRADUATE DEGREE, full-time'; the programme's own 'Key Information' box reads 'Type of course: Second cycle degree (Postgraduate)'. Nominal duration 2 years, 120 ECTS. apply.unito.it: 'Nominal duration: 2 years. For each year of enrollment, students may choose between full-time or part-time status. Tuition fees vary accordingly. (120 ECTS)'. Graduation qualifies holders to sit the Italian State exam for enrolment in section 'A' of the National Register of Biologists, and to enter PhD schools and (where opened to LM-6 graduates) Medical Specialty Schools.
teaching_language: Case 1 - fully English-taught. The whole two-year degree is delivered in English. apply.unito.it (course 345) lists 'Study language: English', and the programme describes itself as 'a two year postgraduate degree entirely taught in English'. It is a SINGLE-UNIVERSITY UNITO degree - NOT an interuniversity/joint degree and NOT an English pathway or curriculum inside an Italian-named degree (the Italian name 'Biologia Cellulare e Molecolare' is simply the mandatory Italian rendering of the same single degree in the national register). Note that four UNITO departments contribute teaching staff and facilities - Life Sciences and Systems Biology (lead), Biological and Clinical Sciences, Drug Science and Technology, and Neurosciences - but these are all internal UNITO departments, so this does not make the degree interuniversity. No Italian-language requirement is published for admission or for graduation; UNITO offers optional 'Learning Italian' courses as a service only. English is required only at CEFR B1 and is verified orally at the admission interview rather than by certificate (see language_requirements).
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. apply.unito.it: 'Study location: Italy, Turin'; the programme's Key Information box: 'Teaching seat: Turin'. Lead department: Department of Life Sciences and Systems Biology (DBIOS), Turin. School: School of Natural Sciences (Scuola di Scienze della Natura). Programme office telephone 011 670 4585. Teaching and admission-test venues named on the programme's 'How to apply' page are in central Turin: the Morphological Laboratory of the Department of Life Sciences and Systems Biology, Via Accademia Albertina 13, and the 'Spallanzani' Room, Via Carlo Alberto 10. University central address: Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino.
degree_class: LM-6 - Biologia (Biology). Confirmed by the UNITO catalogue entry for [2201M22] and corroborated by the programme's own objectives text on apply.unito.it, which refers to 'Specialty Schools pertaining to the School of Medicine, possibly opened to people graduated in LM-6 class'. UNITO internal programme code: [2201M22]. MUR codicione: 0010107300700011. 120 ECTS over 2 years.
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero / 'Course without restricted number of places') BUT with a COMPULSORY TWO-STEP QUALIFYING SELECTION that must be passed before enrolment: (1) a written multiple-choice admission test, and (2) an interview. The programme's Key Information box states 'Entry requirements: Course without restricted number of places', yet its Admission Requirements page states: 'In order to be admitted to the Master in Cellular and Molecular Biology, applicants must pass a test that consists of two steps, a written test and an interview.' There is therefore NO numerus clausus ranking, but there IS a pass/fail gate - the Master Admission Committee issues an 'admission'/'non-admission' judgement based on the curriculum evaluation plus the test result. No TOLC, SAT, GRE or GMAT is used. Two application routes exist: (a) applicants holding a FOREIGN degree (any citizenship) apply through the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course 345); (b) applicants holding an ITALIAN qualification apply through the UNITO portal / MyUniTo using 'Iscrizioni > Pre-iscrizione ai corsi ad accesso libero' and submit an online application for curricular check. A single territorial cap applies: apply.unito.it, 'Territory requirements: This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.'

entry_exam_or_test:
YES - a compulsory TWO-STEP selection consisting of a written test followed by an interview. There is no TOLC, SAT, GRE or GMAT.

STEP 1 - WRITTEN TEST: delivered on the programme's own Moodle platform (https://cmb.i-learn.unito.it/). Format per the Admission Requirements page: '60 multiple choice questions in sequential order (i.e. with no possibility to go back to previous questions) to be taken in 70 minutes.' Subject breakdown: Anatomy/Histology 6 questions; Biochemistry 10; Cell Biology 10; Genetics 8; Microbiology 8; Molecular Biology 10; Physiology 8. 'The multiple choice questions will have at least 4 possible answers and a different weight for the calculation of the final score.' The test is written in English. PASS THRESHOLD: 'In order to be admitted to the interview, the student should reach a score corresponding to at least 50% of the maximal score.' PROCTORING: candidates sitting in person are identified by a committee of at least two teachers of the Master course; international candidates sit remotely - 'on the pre-established date and time, they will connect to the webex/zoom platform (the link will be provided in advance). Their identity will be checked through an official document including a picture. They should keep their video and audio activated for the duration of the written test.' The programme publishes a sample entry test (questions only, and questions with correct answers) as downloadable documents on its microsite, e.g. https://cmb.campusnet.unito.it/do/documenti.pl/FillDoc?_id=g535 .

STEP 2 - INTERVIEW: 'For students who pass step 1 (50% of the maximal score reached), the interview will be carried out by a committee formed of at least 2 teachers of the Master course and it will be a discussion about the written test. In order to pass the interview, the applicant should be able to: Discuss the motivation behind the answers given in the written test and, Demonstrate adequate level of English proficiency.' The interview therefore doubles as the English-language check.

MODALITY AND DATES: tests and interviews are held IN PERSON for candidates with an Italian qualification and REMOTELY for international candidates. In the 2024/25 cycle two in-person sessions were scheduled - 5 September 2024 at 2.00 p.m. (Morphological Laboratory, Department of Life Sciences and Systems Biology, Via A. Albertina 13) and 17 September 2024 at 2.00 p.m. ('Spallanzani' Room, Via Carlo Alberto 10) - while the dates for international candidates were rescheduled and postponed 'due to the large number of applications received'. The equivalent 2026/27 test dates are not published on any page reachable from this environment. [uncertain - the 2026/27 test and interview dates could not be verified; the format, subject breakdown and 50% threshold come from the microsite version last updated 29/01/2025 and are reproduced by live search-engine renderings of the same page, which now carries the heading 'ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS A.A. 2026/27']
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION: 'Possession of a Bachelor Degree (three-year first level degree) achieved in Italy (DM 509; DM 270) or other equivalent qualifications obtained from a foreign University and recognized as satisfactory by the Master Admission Committee'. apply.unito.it phrases the same requirement as: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education.' Candidates still completing their bachelor's may apply (they upload a self-declaration of their study plan with marks, credits and SSD codes) and must graduate by the enrolment deadline - in the 2024/25 cycle 'Admitted candidates must enroll online by January 17, 2025.'

MINIMUM FINAL GRADE - SOURCES DISAGREE: apply.unito.it for a.y. 2026/27 (portal record last updated 23 June 2026) states 'applicants must hold and [sic] undergraduate degree with a final grade equal to or exceeding 8.3/10 of the highest possible grade (92/110 for an Italian degree)'. The programme microsite's Admission Requirements page (version last updated 29/01/2025, headed 'ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS A.A. 2024/25') sets the bar higher, at 'a final grade equal to or exceeding 9.1/10 of the highest possible grade' (i.e. about 100/110). Live search-engine renderings of that microsite page still surface the 9.1/10 figure even though the page heading has been updated to 2026/27. Treat 92/110 (8.3/10) as the operative 2026/27 minimum for Apply@UniTo applicants, because apply.unito.it is the more recently updated official source and is the binding portal for foreign-degree applicants, but verify with the programme office before relying on it. [uncertain - genuine conflict between two official UNITO sources]

DISCIPLINARY BACKGROUND: 'Candidates holding an Italian Bachelor Degree other than L13-Biological Sciences or L2-Biotechnology must possess at least 60 credits in one or more of the following scientific areas (SSD): BIO/01, BIO/02, BIO/03, BIO/04, BIO/05, BIO/06, BIO/07, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/12, BIO/14, BIO/16, BIO/18, BIO/19, CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, FIS/01-08, MAT/01-09, INF/01, ING-INF/05, MED/04, MED/42.' Graduates of Italian classes L-13 (Biological Sciences) and L-2 (Biotechnology) are exempt from this specific 60-CFU count but are NOT exempt from the admission test - unlike some sister UNITO programmes, this degree publishes no test exemption for any category.

SUBJECT KNOWLEDGE ASSESSED (the published syllabus, applying to all applicants including foreign-degree holders; apply.unito.it: 'Applicants should possess basic knowledge of the subjects indicated below. This will be verified by means of an online test and by an interview'):
- Anatomy and Physiology: structure and function of the cardiovascular, digestive, respiratory, excretory, genital endocrine and nervous systems; structure and function of biological membranes; diffusion fluxes.
- Biochemistry: structure and function of proteins (allosteric regulation); enzymes - basic concepts and mechanisms of enzymatic catalysis; principles of bioenergetics and metabolic pathways; basic methods for purification and characterization of proteins.
- Cell Biology: cell communication and signal transduction; cell junction and adhesion; regulation of the cell cycle; cell death and survival; protein trafficking; basic cell culture techniques.
- Cytology and Histology: structure and function of the eukaryotic cell (plasma membrane, organelles, mitosis, meiosis); characteristics and functions of the main tissues (epithelial, connective, muscular, nervous); immunohistochemistry.
- English Language: CEFR B1 level.
- Laboratory skills: preparation of solutions; methods for solution and dilution; laboratory safety.
- Microbiology: structure and function of the prokaryotic cell; microbial metabolism, growth and genetics; methods for cultivation, quantification and identification of bacteria; viruses - structures and replication strategies.
- Molecular Biology and Genetics: DNA and RNA structures; structure of genomes; replication, mutation and DNA repair; transcription, RNA processing and protein synthesis; regulation of gene expression; basic recombinant DNA techniques; genetic recombination and heredity; fundamentals of population genetics; basic bioinformatics.
The microsite publishes a recommended reading list for each syllabus area (Alberts 'Essential Cell Biology'; Nelson & Cox 'Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry' or Mathews/Berg/Voet equivalents; Brock 'Biology of Microorganisms'; Kerr 'Functional Histology'; Watson 'Recombinant DNA'; Brown 'Introduction to Genetics'; Saladin 'Human Anatomy'; Willmer 'Environmental Physiology of Animals').

QUOTA / PLACES: no overall numerus clausus ('Course without restricted number of places'). The only published cap is territorial: 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' No EU sub-quota and no total intake figure is published.

SELECTION DECISION: 'Submitted document evaluation will select candidates fulfilling admission requirements 1 and 2, that will be allowed to participate to the Admission test to assess their academic background (admission requirement 3)'; and 'Based on the evaluation of candidate's curriculum studiorum, as well as on the result of the Admission test, the Master Admission Committee will formulate an admission/non-admission judgement.'

STRUCTURE: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time or part-time status electable for each year of enrolment. Core competences in biochemistry, cell and molecular biology, pharmacology and physiology, plus statistics and IT tools for experimental data collection and analysis, followed by specialisation and an experimental thesis.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH ONLY - no Italian language requirement is published (the degree is fully English-taught).

REQUIRED LEVEL: CEFR B1 - notably LOWER than the B2 required by most UNITO English-taught master's programmes.

NO CERTIFICATE REQUIRED. This is the programme's most distinctive admission feature and it is stated explicitly on the microsite's syllabus section: 'English Language - Your knowledge of the English language, comparable to a B1 level (no need of certification), will be verified during the admission interview.' apply.unito.it states the same for its (foreign-degree) applicant pool under 'Language requirements: English - Your knowledge of the English language (at least B1 level) will be verified during the admission interview', and lists 'English Language: Common European Framework (CEF) B1 level' among the subject areas assessed. There is therefore NO published list of accepted certificates and no minimum IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge score for this programme; the assessment is made orally by the admission committee, which must be satisfied that the applicant can 'Demonstrate adequate level of English proficiency' during the interview discussion of the written test.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: applicants without an English certificate are not excluded, but they carry the whole language burden into a live interview conducted in English by at least two members of teaching staff. Applicants who do hold a certificate may upload it as supporting documentation, but no official page makes it mandatory or defines a threshold. [uncertain - because no certificate list is published, it cannot be ruled out that the Apply@UniTo assessors informally expect documentary evidence from applicants whose prior degree was not English-taught; this is not addressed on any official page]
required_documents:
A) APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN DEGREE - via the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course 345). The programme's own microsite routes them here: 'Students with foreign title must apply through the on-line form.'
1. Valid identity document / passport (passport for non-EU citizens).
2. First-cycle (bachelor's) degree certificate obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent/higher qualification. If not yet awarded, evidence that it will be obtained by the enrolment deadline.
3. Official academic transcript of records showing exams, credits (CFU/ECTS) and grades, so that the subject-background requirement and the minimum final grade (92/110 = 8.3/10 per apply.unito.it) can be verified.
4. MOTIVATION LETTER in English or Italian - explicitly required on the course page ('Other requirements: A motivation letter must be added to your application') and listed by Apply@UniTo as mandatory for all postgraduate programmes.
5. NO English language certificate is required for this programme (English B1 is verified at the interview instead) - unlike most other UNITO English-taught master's programmes.
6. Optional but recommended: degree programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign institution, with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish.
7. Payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call (same amount whether one or two degree programmes are selected).
LANGUAGE OF DOCUMENTS: 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.'
AFTER SUBMISSION: UNITO may request further documents such as a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore), a Statement of Verification, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability; the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment stage.

B) APPLICANTS WITH AN ITALIAN QUALIFICATION - via the UNITO portal / MyUniTo ('Iscrizioni > Pre-iscrizione ai corsi ad accesso libero'), submitting an online application for curricular check:
- Already graduated: 'fill the portal registration form on the Unito website and submit the application for curricular check online, upload a self-declaration testifying the possession of the Bachelor Degree, specifying each discipline with marks.'
- Still undergraduate: 'fill the portal registration form on the Unito website for curricular check online and upload a self-declaration testifying the study plan including for each discipline: marks, university credit number, scientific disciplinary sector (SSD).'
- Candidates from other Italian universities must first register at the UNITO portal as a 'Future student' before accessing the pre-enrolment menu.

C) ALL CANDIDATES: sit the written admission test (score at least 50% of the maximum to advance) and then pass the interview. Admitted candidates must complete online enrolment by the published deadline (17 January 2025 in the 2024/25 cycle).
[uncertain - list B, the curricular-check wording and the enrolment deadline were read from the microsite versions archived at 16/05/2024 and 29/01/2025; the 2026/27 versions of those pages could not be opened directly]

ACCESS PROBLEMS DURING RESEARCH (2026-09-01): (1) apply.unito.it refused the WebFetch tool but was fully retrievable with a standard desktop browser user-agent via curl - it is the primary verified source for this record, and its machine-readable feed (course 345, JSON v1, portal record last updated 2026-06-23) independently confirms both 2026/27 intakes and their deadlines. (2) The programme microsite cmb.campusnet.unito.it (host 130.186.3.24, shared with dbiosen.campusnet.unito.it) refused every direct connection over both http and https, from curl, from WebFetch and through three public CORS proxies; r.jina.ai returned a Cloudflare challenge; no alternative host (cmb.unito.it, www.cmb.unito.it) resolves. Its Admission Requirements, How to apply, home and Tuition pages were therefore recovered from Wayback Machine raw (id_) snapshots 20250315050154, 20240810232758, 20260505165232 and 20230515044516, fetched over plain http; archive.org rate-limited this session with HTTP 429 after several requests and its CDX endpoint was unreachable, so no newer snapshots could be enumerated. (3) en.unito.it, www.unito.it and unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it all return HTTP 403 or a bot challenge; content from those hosts is reported from search-engine renderings only and is flagged as such. (4) polito.it (Politecnico di Torino) was correctly excluded as out of scope; no polito.it source was consulted.

MOST IMPORTANT CONFLICT - MINIMUM FINAL GRADE: apply.unito.it for 2026/27 (portal record updated 23 June 2026) requires 'a final grade equal to or exceeding 8.3/10 of the highest possible grade (92/110 for an Italian degree)', whereas the programme microsite's Admission Requirements page requires '9.1/10 of the highest possible grade' (roughly 100/110). The archived microsite version is headed 'ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS A.A. 2024/25' (last update 29/01/2025), but live search-engine renderings of the same URL now show the heading 'admission requirements a.a. 2026/27' while still surfacing the 9.1/10 figure - so it is not possible to tell from outside whether the microsite figure is simply stale or whether the two routes genuinely apply different bars. This record treats 92/110 (8.3/10) as the operative threshold for Apply@UniTo (foreign-degree) applicants because that source is the more recently updated and is the binding portal for them, but an applicant sitting between 92/110 and 100/110 MUST confirm with the programme before relying on it.

CYCLE-CURRENCY CAVEAT: the recovered microsite snapshots carry 2024/25 content for the selection rules and the application windows. The subject syllabus, the 60-question/70-minute test format, the 50%-of-maximum threshold for advancing to the interview, the 60-CFU/SSD rule and the 'B1, no certification needed' language rule are all reproduced verbatim by apply.unito.it for 2026/27 and by live renderings of the microsite, so they are very likely current. By contrast, the DOMESTIC application windows (3 July - 26 August 2024 and 3 July - 5 September 2024), the ADMISSION TEST DATES (5 and 17 September 2024, 2.00 p.m.) and the ENROLMENT DEADLINE (17 January 2025) are certainly year-specific and the 2026/27 equivalents could not be found on any reachable page. Applicants must check the microsite's 'How to apply' page for the 2026/27 test calendar.

FIELD-LEVEL UNCERTAINTIES: (a) academic_requirements - the 8.3/10 vs 9.1/10 conflict described above; also, the 60-CFU/SSD threshold is written only for holders of an ITALIAN bachelor degree outside classes L-13 and L-2, and no numeric credit equivalent is published anywhere for foreign-degree holders, whose background is assessed qualitatively by the Master Admission Committee against the published syllabus. (b) entry_exam_or_test - the 2026/27 test and interview dates are unknown; the modality split (in person for Italian-qualification candidates, remote via webex/zoom for international candidates) is from the 2024/25 page and, in that cycle, the international dates were explicitly 'rescheduled and postponed' because of application volume, so international candidates should not assume the published Italian dates apply to them. (c) application_deadline_eu / application_deadline_non_eu - the Apply@UniTo dates (8 September 2026 and 29 January 2026) are directly verified, but the domestic UNITO-portal window for Italian-qualification candidates is not, and the Universitaly visa pre-enrolment deadline for non-EU candidates is a separate national requirement not mentioned on this programme's pages. (d) language_requirements - unusually for UNITO, NO English certificate is required and NO accepted-certificate list or minimum score exists; the entire language check is an oral judgement made at the admission interview against a B1 benchmark. This is a genuine finding, quoted verbatim from two independent official sources, but it means there is no documentary safe harbour for an applicant, and it cannot be ruled out that assessors informally expect evidence from applicants without an English-medium background. (e) required_documents - the domestic (Italian-qualification) document list and the 'curricular check' procedure are from the microsite version last updated 16/05/2024. (f) tuition_or_fees_link - the EUR 156-2,800 range is explicitly the a.y. 2025-26 figure carried on apply.unito.it; the 2026-27 bands were not yet published. (g) teaching_language - fully English is firmly established; the only nuance is that four UNITO departments contribute to the degree, which is an internal organisational arrangement and does NOT make it an interuniversity/joint degree.

TERMINOLOGICAL WARNING FOR DOWNSTREAM USE: this programme is officially labelled 'course without restricted number of places' / 'Access: free', but it must NOT be presented to applicants as automatic or open entry. Enrolment is impossible without passing BOTH a weighted 60-question written test (>= 50% of the maximum score) AND a subsequent oral interview with at least two members of teaching staff, and non-EU applicants residing abroad additionally compete within a hard cap of 50 places. In practice it is a selective admission that merely lacks a ranked quota.
